DQ_DIRECTION_UNCERTAIN.title: Credit or debit direction uncertain
DQ_DIRECTION_UNCERTAIN.meaning: The parser could not tell, for a row, whether the amount is a credit or a debit.
DQ_DIRECTION_UNCERTAIN.why: A wrong direction distorts the balance and deposit checks, so the system trusts its reading less.
DQ_DIRECTION_UNCERTAIN.confirm: Open the page and compare the row with the money in and money out columns and with the running balance.
DQ_DIRECTION_UNCERTAIN.false_alarms: Statements that print amounts without a column or a sign.

DQ_LAYOUT_UNRECOGNISED.title: Statement layout not recognised
DQ_LAYOUT_UNRECOGNISED.meaning: The page layout did not match a known statement layout, or reading the page failed.
DQ_LAYOUT_UNRECOGNISED.why: Rows may be missing or misread, which weakens every later check.
DQ_LAYOUT_UNRECOGNISED.confirm: Open the PDF and check whether the page is an ordinary bank statement table. If it is a scan or photo, ask for the bank's original digital statement.
DQ_LAYOUT_UNRECOGNISED.false_alarms: A new bank layout the parser has not seen before.

DQ_MISSING_HOLDER.title: Account holder missing
DQ_MISSING_HOLDER.meaning: The statement header did not yield the account holder name.
DQ_MISSING_HOLDER.why: The name cannot be compared with the company registry.
DQ_MISSING_HOLDER.confirm: Look for the account holder on the first page of the PDF. If it is truly absent, ask for a complete statement.

DQ_MISSING_OPENING.title: Opening balance missing
DQ_MISSING_OPENING.meaning: The statement header did not yield an opening balance.
DQ_MISSING_OPENING.why: The running balance cannot be reconciled from the start.
DQ_MISSING_OPENING.confirm: Look for the opening balance on the first page, or compare with the previous month's closing balance.

DQ_MISSING_PERIOD.title: Statement period missing
DQ_MISSING_PERIOD.meaning: The statement header did not yield a statement period.
DQ_MISSING_PERIOD.why: Coverage and gap checks cannot run without dates.
DQ_MISSING_PERIOD.confirm: Look for the statement period on the first page of the PDF, or ask for a complete statement.

DQ_MISSING_UEN.title: UEN missing
DQ_MISSING_UEN.meaning: The statement header did not yield a company UEN.
DQ_MISSING_UEN.why: The company registry check cannot run.
DQ_MISSING_UEN.confirm: Look for the UEN on the first page of the PDF and check it on the official registry by hand.

DQ_NO_TEXT.title: No extractable text
DQ_NO_TEXT.meaning: No text could be taken from the PDF. It may be an image or an empty file.
DQ_NO_TEXT.why: Nothing can be checked, so every other result is weak.
DQ_NO_TEXT.confirm: Open the PDF. If it is a scan or photo, ask for the bank's original digital statement.

DQ_NO_TXNS.title: No transactions parsed
DQ_NO_TXNS.meaning: No transaction rows could be read from the statement.
DQ_NO_TXNS.why: There is little to base any judgement on, so confidence drops sharply.
DQ_NO_TXNS.confirm: Check whether the PDF contains a transaction table and ask for the full statement if it does not.

DQ_PARSE_INCONSISTENT.title: Printed total differs from parsed rows
DQ_PARSE_INCONSISTENT.meaning: Every running balance reconciles row by row, but a printed section total differs from the sum of the parsed rows.
DQ_PARSE_INCONSISTENT.why: This points to a reading mistake by the system more than to document fraud, so it lowers confidence only a little.
DQ_PARSE_INCONSISTENT.confirm: Compare the printed totals with the rows on the same page.

DQ_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE.title: Company registry could not be checked
DQ_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE.meaning: The company registry could not be reached or did not answer, for example because of a network problem.
DQ_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE.why: This says nothing about the company. The registry check was skipped.
DQ_REGISTRY_UNAVAILABLE.confirm: Screen the statement again later, or check the UEN on the official registry by hand.

DQ_RULE_SKIPPED.title: A fabrication check was skipped
DQ_RULE_SKIPPED.meaning: One of the invoice or turnover checks could not run, for example because the data it needs is missing.
DQ_RULE_SKIPPED.why: That area was not checked by the system.
DQ_RULE_SKIPPED.confirm: Review the invoice references and the turnover pattern by hand.

DQ_UNREADABLE_ROW.title: Unreadable transaction row
DQ_UNREADABLE_ROW.meaning: A transaction row could not be read.
DQ_UNREADABLE_ROW.why: The row is missing from the checks, which can hide a problem.
DQ_UNREADABLE_ROW.confirm: Open the page, read the row, and check that the running balance still adds up around it.

FL_BALANCE_BREAK.title: Running balance does not reconcile
FL_BALANCE_BREAK.meaning: The printed running balance is not the previous balance plus the row amount.
FL_BALANCE_BREAK.why: This is a classic sign that an amount or a balance was edited.
FL_BALANCE_BREAK.confirm: Recalculate the balance around the row, compare with the bank's own copy of the statement, and look at the font of the figures on that row.
FL_BALANCE_BREAK.false_alarms: A row the parser read in the wrong direction (see DQ_DIRECTION_UNCERTAIN).

FL_CLOSING_MISMATCH.title: Closing balance disagrees with last row
FL_CLOSING_MISMATCH.meaning: The printed closing balance differs from the balance on the last transaction row.
FL_CLOSING_MISMATCH.why: Rows may have been added or removed after the balance was printed.
FL_CLOSING_MISMATCH.confirm: Compare the closing balance with the last row and with the next month's opening balance.

FL_DUP_INVOICE_REF.title: Invoice reference paid more than once
FL_DUP_INVOICE_REF.meaning: The same invoice reference appears in more than one incoming payment.
FL_DUP_INVOICE_REF.why: Repeated or invented credits can inflate turnover.
FL_DUP_INVOICE_REF.confirm: Ask for the invoice and the payment advice, and check whether the payments are genuine instalments.
FL_DUP_INVOICE_REF.false_alarms: Instalments of one invoice, or a payer who quotes one reference on several invoices.

FL_INVOICE_SEQUENCE_BREAK.title: Invoice numbers out of date order
FL_INVOICE_SEQUENCE_BREAK.meaning: Invoice numbers in the payments do not rise with the dates.
FL_INVOICE_SEQUENCE_BREAK.why: Numbers may have been invented. This is a weak signal.
FL_INVOICE_SEQUENCE_BREAK.confirm: Ask for the applicant's invoice register and compare the numbers.
FL_INVOICE_SEQUENCE_BREAK.false_alarms: Customers who pay older invoices late.

FL_MONTH_DUPLICATE.title: Duplicate or overlapping month
FL_MONTH_DUPLICATE.meaning: A month appears more than once, or two statement sections overlap.
FL_MONTH_DUPLICATE.why: The same month may have been submitted twice or relabelled to cover a missing month.
FL_MONTH_DUPLICATE.confirm: Compare the month headers and page ranges of each section and check the balances at the joins.

FL_MONTH_MISSING.title: Missing month
FL_MONTH_MISSING.meaning: A month inside the covered range has no statement.
FL_MONTH_MISSING.why: The missing month may hide activity.
FL_MONTH_MISSING.confirm: Ask the applicant for the missing month, ideally straight from the bank.

FL_MONTH_OUT_OF_ORDER.title: Months out of order
FL_MONTH_OUT_OF_ORDER.meaning: Statement months are not in chronological order.
FL_MONTH_OUT_OF_ORDER.why: Pages may have been reordered or stitched together from different documents.
FL_MONTH_OUT_OF_ORDER.confirm: Check the page order and the balances where one month meets the next.

FL_PERIOD_GAP.title: Unexplained gap in the statement period
FL_PERIOD_GAP.meaning: A stretch with no transactions is longer than this company's normal pace.
FL_PERIOD_GAP.why: Pages or activity may have been removed.
FL_PERIOD_GAP.confirm: Check the page numbers and balances on either side of the gap and ask the applicant to explain the quiet period.

FL_PERIOD_LENGTH.title: Statement period outside the 6 to 12 month window
FL_PERIOD_LENGTH.meaning: The statements do not cover between 6 and 12 months, which is the requirement for a corporate loan.
FL_PERIOD_LENGTH.why: The application does not meet the document requirement as submitted.
FL_PERIOD_LENGTH.confirm: Check the first and last dates of the statement and ask for the right number of months.

FL_RAPID_PASS_THROUGH.title: Large credits leave the account again within days
FL_RAPID_PASS_THROUGH.meaning: Large incoming amounts are followed by similar outgoing amounts within days.
FL_RAPID_PASS_THROUGH.why: Money that only passes through an account can point to circular funds or to turnover that is not real.
FL_RAPID_PASS_THROUGH.confirm: Trace the counterparties on both sides and ask for the contract or invoice behind the transfers.
FL_RAPID_PASS_THROUGH.false_alarms: Trading businesses that pay suppliers as soon as customers pay them.

FL_STRUCTURING.title: Possible structuring below the reporting threshold
FL_STRUCTURING.meaning: Several deposits sit just under the reporting threshold.
FL_STRUCTURING.why: Splitting cash to stay below a threshold is a known way to avoid reporting.
FL_STRUCTURING.confirm: Ask who made the deposits and why they were split, and compare with the company's usual way of being paid.
FL_STRUCTURING.false_alarms: Regular takings that happen to be small.

FL_SUDDEN_DEPOSIT.title: Deposit unusually large for this company
FL_SUDDEN_DEPOSIT.meaning: A single credit is far larger than this company's normal credits.
FL_SUDDEN_DEPOSIT.why: It may be an invented or borrowed amount that makes the account look stronger.
FL_SUDDEN_DEPOSIT.confirm: Ask for the invoice or contract behind it and check who the payer is.

FL_TURNOVER_COST_MISMATCH.title: Turnover jumps while fixed costs stay flat
FL_TURNOVER_COST_MISMATCH.meaning: Monthly credits rise sharply while payroll and rent-type costs stay the same.
FL_TURNOVER_COST_MISMATCH.confirm: Compare the turnover with other records such as invoices and tax filings.

FL_UEN_NAME_MISMATCH.title: Account holder does not match the registry
FL_UEN_NAME_MISMATCH.meaning: The account holder printed on the statement differs from the registered name for the UEN.
FL_UEN_NAME_MISMATCH.why: The statement may belong to a different company.
FL_UEN_NAME_MISMATCH.confirm: Compare the printed name and UEN with the official registry entry and ask the applicant to explain any name change.
FL_UEN_NAME_MISMATCH.false_alarms: Trading names and recent name changes.

FL_UEN_NOT_FOUND.title: UEN not found in the registry
FL_UEN_NOT_FOUND.meaning: The UEN is not in the registry that was checked.
FL_UEN_NOT_FOUND.why: The company may not exist under that number, or the number may be mistyped.
FL_UEN_NOT_FOUND.confirm: Check the UEN on the official registry by hand.

FL_UNVERIFIED_COUNTERPARTY.title: Large inflow from a payer not seen before
FL_UNVERIFIED_COUNTERPARTY.meaning: A large credit came from a payer that does not appear in the company's usual counterparties.
FL_UNVERIFIED_COUNTERPARTY.why: Funds from unknown or shell-like payers can make an account look busier than it is.
FL_UNVERIFIED_COUNTERPARTY.confirm: Identify the payer and the reason for the payment, and check whether payer and applicant are related.

MEM_HIGH_FREQUENCY_PATTERN.title: Counterparty and amount recur across many prior cases
MEM_HIGH_FREQUENCY_PATTERN.meaning: The same counterparty and amount band appear in many earlier cases that people decided.
MEM_HIGH_FREQUENCY_PATTERN.why: A party that keeps appearing across applications is worth a closer look.
MEM_HIGH_FREQUENCY_PATTERN.confirm: Read the cited earlier cases and see whether the same party keeps appearing.

MEM_RECURRING_KNOWN_BAD.title: Transaction matches one in a rejected case
MEM_RECURRING_KNOWN_BAD.meaning: A suspicious transaction matches one from an earlier case that a human reviewer rejected.
MEM_RECURRING_KNOWN_BAD.why: It is a repeat of a pattern already judged bad.
MEM_RECURRING_KNOWN_BAD.confirm: Read the cited earlier case and the reviewer's reason before deciding.

MEM_SIMILAR_PASSED_BEFORE.title: Similar transaction passed in an earlier case
MEM_SIMILAR_PASSED_BEFORE.meaning: A similar transaction was cleared by a human reviewer in an earlier case.
MEM_SIMILAR_PASSED_BEFORE.why: A route that passed once may be reused on purpose.
MEM_SIMILAR_PASSED_BEFORE.confirm: Read the cited earlier case and check what was explained or different then.

ML_STATEMENT_FORGERY_LIKELIHOOD.title: Model flags elevated statement-forgery likelihood
ML_STATEMENT_FORGERY_LIKELIHOOD.meaning: A trained model scores the whole document as more likely to be tampered, from file-level features such as fonts, editor traces and balance reconciliation.
ML_STATEMENT_FORGERY_LIKELIHOOD.why: It is a second opinion on the document as a whole.
ML_STATEMENT_FORGERY_LIKELIHOOD.confirm: Compare with the rule-based findings for the same document. The model is a prompt to look, not proof.

ML_TXN_FRAUD_LIKELIHOOD.title: Model flags elevated transaction-fraud likelihood
ML_TXN_FRAUD_LIKELIHOOD.meaning: A trained model scores a transaction as more likely to be fraudulent.
ML_TXN_FRAUD_LIKELIHOOD.why: It may catch patterns the rules do not, but it can also mistake ordinary business amounts for fraud.
ML_TXN_FRAUD_LIKELIHOOD.confirm: Look at the flagged row and its counterparty. The score is a prompt to look, not proof.

ML_TXN_GNN_RISK.title: Graph model flags elevated account-level risk
ML_TXN_GNN_RISK.meaning: A graph model marks the account as risky from patterns across accounts, such as round-tripping or many-to-one and one-to-many flows.
ML_TXN_GNN_RISK.why: It sees relationships that a single row cannot show.
ML_TXN_GNN_RISK.confirm: Review the account's main counterparties and money flows.

SEC_EMBEDDED_INSTRUCTION.title: Embedded instruction detected in document text
SEC_EMBEDDED_INSTRUCTION.meaning: Text inside the document tries to give orders to the screening system. It is never obeyed.
SEC_EMBEDDED_INSTRUCTION.why: A genuine bank statement does not contain such text, so the attempt itself is strong evidence of tampering.
SEC_EMBEDDED_INSTRUCTION.confirm: Open the page named in the finding, look at the text and at how it was hidden, and treat the whole document as suspect.

VF_CREATION_BEFORE_PERIOD.title: Document created before the statement period
VF_CREATION_BEFORE_PERIOD.meaning: The file's creation date is earlier than the period the statement covers.
VF_CREATION_BEFORE_PERIOD.why: A genuine statement cannot exist before the period it reports has happened.
VF_CREATION_BEFORE_PERIOD.confirm: Compare the creation date in the document properties with the statement period and ask the bank for the original.

VF_CURRENCY_MIX.title: Inconsistent currency notation
VF_CURRENCY_MIX.meaning: The amounts use more than one currency notation.
VF_CURRENCY_MIX.why: Rows may have been spliced in from another document.
VF_CURRENCY_MIX.confirm: Look down the amounts column for different symbols or formats.

VF_DATE_FORMAT_MIX.title: Inconsistent date formats
VF_DATE_FORMAT_MIX.meaning: More than one date format is used inside one statement.
VF_DATE_FORMAT_MIX.why: Rows may have been edited or spliced in.
VF_DATE_FORMAT_MIX.confirm: Look down the date column for rows that are written differently from the rest.

VF_EDIT_SOFTWARE.title: Editing software trace in metadata
VF_EDIT_SOFTWARE.meaning: The document properties name image or PDF editing software.
VF_EDIT_SOFTWARE.why: Banks produce statements with their own systems, not with editing tools.
VF_EDIT_SOFTWARE.confirm: Check the producer and creator in the document properties and ask for the original from the bank.
VF_EDIT_SOFTWARE.false_alarms: A scan or print step done by the applicant.

VF_FONT_MISMATCH.title: Localised font inconsistency
VF_FONT_MISMATCH.meaning: A small patch of text uses a different font from the rest of the page.
VF_FONT_MISMATCH.why: This is a classic sign of overwritten numbers.
VF_FONT_MISMATCH.confirm: Zoom in on the page and compare the font of the flagged figures with the figures around them.

VF_MODIFIED_AFTER_CREATION.title: File changed after it was created
VF_MODIFIED_AFTER_CREATION.meaning: The file was modified after creation by something other than a print or export tool.
VF_MODIFIED_AFTER_CREATION.why: A statement downloaded from a bank is normally not edited afterwards.
VF_MODIFIED_AFTER_CREATION.confirm: Compare the creation and modification dates and check which tool made the last change.
